messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's spike in eu-west we saw ~20% queue increase and a few 503s. I tried a quick prealloc tweak but want a second pair of eyes on an admission smoothing plan.

kevin: Saw it on the charts. queued_requests peaked ~630, warm_provision_time ~38s. Region constraints + sudden burst from a customer caused it.

oliver: Logs show prealloc_count hit 0 for a short window, then mass node starts. Also noticed model fetch added ~8-10s to instance warm time.

tara: I increased max_burst_tokens from 200 -> 500 yesterday which reduced 503s but bumped spend on Dedicated pools. Not sustainable for long.

maria: Thinking we should move from an immediate refill to a smoothing + decaying headroom approach. Pseudo-config idea: 

```yaml
prealloc:
  target_percent: 0.15   # keep ~15% of pool preallocated
  headroom_decay_tau_s: 120
admission:
  smoothing_window_s: 30
  max_rate_per_gpu: 12
  burst_tokens: 400
```

kevin: That looks reasonable. Suggest adding exponential backoff on consecutive refills so we don't thrash the autoscaler. e.g., after each refill within X minutes, double the wait.

oliver: Also: model blob caching on local SSD would cut ~8s off warm_provision_time. If warm time is lower, prealloc target can shrink. Worth a ticket.

tara: Reminder: extra prealloc ~+7% monthly GPU hours in our cost model. Enterprise customers on fixed reserved capacity will complain if we just blanket increase headroom.

maria: Proposal: implement adaptive prealloc tied to a rolling 5m qps percentile plus a "cost cap" override. If cost cap breached, automatically tighten headroom and shift to stricter admission (queue backpressure -> 429) instead of spinning new nodes.

kevin: Dashboard/alert changes to support this: add prealloc_headroom, next_refill_ts, burst_token_balance. New pager rule: queue_depth > 400 for 2m AND prealloc_headroom < 10 -> pager.

sre-bot: deploy scheduled — canary rollout to 10% of clusters at 1785004444.

maria: Rollout plan I'm thinking: 1) feature-flag off; 2) enable smoothing + adaptive headroom on canary clusters; 3) run synthetic traffic 15m; 4) observe latency, queue, cost delta; 5) ramp if green. Any objections?

oliver: No objections. Add emergency rollback: set target_percent=0 and flush burst_tokens to avoid extra spend.

tara: Also add a cost sim step: `python infra/sim/prealloc_sim.py --qps=... --duration=1h` before ramping to estimate GPU-hour delta.

kevin: I'll attach the synthetic-runbook + dashboards and add the pager threshold.

maria: Thanks — I'll open the PR with config + runbook and tag you all. :thumbsup:
